title: The Forbidden Embrace
content:
The cool evening breeze of Dagshai carried the scent of pine trees as Siddu, Sneha, and Yashwanth stood silently, admiring the breathtaking landscape before them.

The endless green hills, the mist drifting between the mountains, and the peaceful silence of the quiet hill town left all three of them mesmerized.

For a few moments, none of them spoke.

They simply stood there, taking in the beauty around them.

As night slowly settled over the hills, they made their way to a nearby hotel.

After finishing dinner together, they checked into two rooms.

Sneha took one room for herself, while Siddu and Yashwanth shared the other.

A little later, Sneha gently knocked on their door.

Yashwanth opened it with a smile.

"Come in."

She stepped inside and looked at Siddu.

"So..." she said with an eager smile, "are you going to continue the story?"

Yashwanth immediately sat comfortably on the bed.

"I've heard it before," he laughed, "but I don't mind hearing it again."

Siddu smiled faintly.

He pulled a chair closer and gestured toward Sneha.

"Sit."

Once everyone had settled down, the room became quiet.

Siddu took a deep breath.

"After the principal warned me not to talk to Shreya," he began, "I somehow managed to calm myself."

"I explained everything to Adithya and asked him to convey the situation to Shreya."

"He did."

"From that day onward..."

"...Shreya and I stopped talking completely."

Sneha frowned.

"But... why didn't you both chat on your phones?"

Before Siddu could answer, Yashwanth laughed.

"His parents hardly allowed him to touch his phone back then."

Siddu smiled and nodded.

"That's true."

"So, there was no way for us to stay in touch."

He lowered his eyes.

"The days kept passing..."

"But instead of healing me, every day pushed me deeper into loneliness."

"The only conversations we had..."

"...were through our eyes."

Whenever they crossed paths in the corridors, they would silently look at each other for a few moments before walking away.

No words.

No smiles.

Just silence.

"It hurt more than I can explain."

Siddu paused.

"Meanwhile, the first JEE Main examination was only three and a half months away."

"Everyone around me was studying harder than ever."

"But I..."

He smiled bitterly.

"...couldn't even focus on a single page."

"My body was sitting in the classroom..."

"But my heart was always searching for Shreya."

He looked at Sneha.

"One evening..."

"I finally made a decision."

"I told myself that even if the principal suspended me..."

"...I had to speak to her."

"So, during the evening break, I walked straight toward her classroom."

"The moment Shreya saw me approaching..."

"I could see fear in her eyes."

She hurried toward me and whispered,

"Siddu... have you forgotten what the principal said? If he sees us together, you'll be suspended."

I looked at her and quietly replied,

"You're only thinking about the punishment..."

"...but you're not seeing what I'm going through."

"I've been trying to study."

"I know the JEE exam is only a few months away."

"But no matter how hard I try..."

"I can't concentrate."

"My mind is never at peace."

"I think about you every single day."

"So, I came here..."

"...because I wanted to clear my heart."

For a few seconds...

Shreya didn't say a single word.

She simply looked into my eyes.

Slowly...

Tears began rolling down her cheeks.

Before I could say anything else...

She stepped forward...

...and hugged me tightly.

For the first time in months...

I broke down.

All the pain, loneliness, and helplessness that I had been hiding finally came pouring out as tears.

I hugged her back without caring about the world around us.

For those few precious moments...

Nothing else mattered.

Neither the principal...

Nor the college...

Nor the future...

Only Shreya.

Siddu fell silent.

His eyes slowly lowered.

"That day..."

he whispered,

"was the first time I had cried in front of someone since the day I entered Intermediate."

He paused.

Then a faint, painful smile appeared on his face.

"But..."

"A single unexpected visit..."

"...changed everything."
